claim: A 3.5 mg NaDCC tablet carries 2.0 mg of available chlorine (57% of its mass, anhydrous basis)
law: Stoichiometry: two N-Cl per NaDCC, each counted as one Cl2; IFRC catalogue WASDCHLA01 (2 mg per 3.5 mg tablet)
check: Theory 55.4% (dihydrate) to 64.5% (anhydrous); catalogue tablets 57% to 61%, so the tablets are anhydrous NaDCC with binder

claim: D1: one matched tablet gives about 2 mg/L free chlorine (1 L tablet in 1 L, or 20 L tablet in 20 L; 1.6 mg/L in 25 L)
law: Dose = available chlorine / volume; household tablet doses (IFRC tablet-choice note: 67 mg per 20 to 25 L)
check: 1.6 mg/L >= 1 mg/L

claim: The double dose for settled turbid water (two tablets, 4.0 mg/L) stays at or below the WHO chlorine guideline value of 5 mg/L in the containers on the label (1 to 1.5 L, 20 L)
law: WHO guideline value 5 mg/L (WHO chlorine fact sheet 2022); IFRC: double dose if visibly turbid; bottle range from S42
check: 4 mg/L <= 5 mg/L

claim: Free chlorine after 30 minutes stays at or above the WHO 0.5 mg/L for clear water (under 5 NTU) at the single dose (1.7 mg/L)
law: WHO GDWQ: at least 0.5 mg/L after 30 min at pH under 8 (via WEDC Mobile Note 7); residual model with assumed demand 0.3 mg/L
check: Passes while the 30 minute demand is under 1.5 mg/L; demand is assumed, and Wu and Dorea (2020) measured up to 4 mg/L over 24 h in jerrycans, so real demand is measured (HWP-VER-001 TJ)

claim: A residual remains for a day of storage before filtering: 0.75 mg/L (clear) and 0.58 mg/L (turbid, double dose) at 24 h
law: CDC Safe Water System: above 0.2 mg/L at 24 h (Lantagne 2006); first-order decay after the 30 min demand, k assumed 0.035 and 0.07 per hour
check: 24 h consumption 1.3 and 3.4 mg/L, inside the 0.5 to 4 mg/L measured in 20 L jerrycans (Wu and Dorea 2020); at the top of that range the single dose leaves none; the residual matters only until the water is filtered (S16); real demand to measure (HWP-VER-001 TJ, TD)

claim: A single dose in turbid water keeps a residual for 24 h (it falls to 0.19 mg/L)
law: Same model with turbid demand 1.0 mg/L in 30 min; CDC 0.2 mg/L at 24 h; IFRC: under 5 NTU for proper disinfection, above 50 NTU do not chlorinate
check: Failed as briefed (one tablet for all water). Fixed (F1): settle first and use two tablets for 5 to 50 NTU, do not use above 50 NTU; the double dose leaves 0.58 mg/L at 24 h on an assumed 1.0 mg/L demand; demand at 10, 25 and 50 NTU to measure (TJ)

claim: Water dosed for 30 minutes stays under the CDC 2.0 mg/L acceptability limit at 1 h when clear (1.67 mg/L), but not at the turbid double dose (2.90 mg/L)
law: CDC SWS 2.0 mg/L at 1 h; median taste detection 0.73 and acceptability 1.26 mg/L for NaDCC (Crider et al. 2018)
check: Most users will taste chlorine before filtering; the carbon stages of A to C are intended to remove it, so water is drunk only after the filter; taste after the filter is measured (TG, TH)

claim: In 30 minutes clear water at the single dose reaches the CT for 4-log virus inactivation at 5 C (CT 51 against 8 mg min/L)
law: US EPA CT table for 4-log virus inactivation by free chlorine, pH 6 to 9 (Hepatitis A data with a safety factor of 3); CT = residual at the end of contact x time (EPA definition; the integral gives 53)
check: 51 mg min/L >= 8 mg min/L

claim: No 4-log virus credit is taken above 5 NTU: the misuse case (turbid water, single dose) reaches CT 30 in 30 minutes, but the EPA table assumes low-turbidity water
law: As S8, demand 1.0 mg/L in 30 min; particle-associated viruses are shielded from chlorine, so the CT table is not applied to 5 to 50 NTU water (IFRC: under 5 NTU for proper disinfection)
check: The misuse case is not credited; settled turbid water at the double dose is credited only after the TB challenge at 10 and 50 NTU (HWP-VER-001 TB)

claim: No quantified norovirus claim is made; free chlorine at the household dose is expected to act on human norovirus, but the data are not drinking-water infectivity data
law: Dunkin et al. 2017: 2-log molecular (RT-qPCR) reduction of norovirus GII at CT 7.5 to 13 in produce wash water; no 4-log infectivity data for human norovirus in drinking water
check: CT 51 is 3.9 times the 2-log molecular figure, which is a different measure from infectivity; virus reduction for the combined system is measured, never assumed (HWP-VER-001 TB)

claim: Cold water gets a longer wait: 30 min above 18 C, 60 min at 10 to 18 C, 120 min below 10 C
law: US EPA CT rises from 3 (20 C) to 12 mg min/L (0.5 C); WHO and WEDC TN 11: 30 minutes at 18 C and above; the 60 and 120 minute tiers are practice guidance (Akvopedia NaDCC page, revision of the page)
check: Already at 30 min the CT is 4.2 times the 0.5 C requirement, so the longer cold waits are a conservative margin, not the basis of the virus check; at 120 min the CT is 194, 16 times

claim: Disinfection weakens as pH rises (HOCl share 55% at pH 7.5, 28% at 8.0 at 20 C; 15% at pH 8.5 and 5 C); pH above 8 takes 60 minutes and pH above 9 is excluded
law: HOCl pKa by temperature (Morris 1966): 7.54 at 25 C, 7.58 at 20 C, 7.75 at 5 C; EPA CT table applies to pH 6 to 9 and jumps from 8 to 60 at pH 10; Akvopedia: unreliable above pH 9
check: The check uses the EPA table directly (CT 51 against 8 at pH 6 to 9); HOCl weighting is not applied on top because the table already covers pH; the 60 minute rule above pH 8 is extra margin; field pH to record (TD), source suitability by class (HWP-SRC-001)

claim: Chlorine does not inactivate Cryptosporidium at household doses, so the filter (A to C) is still needed
law: CDC chlorine timetable: about 15,300 min at 1 mg/L, pH 7.5, 25 C; Akvopedia; HWP-CLM-001
check: At 1.7 mg/L the CT would take about 6 days; D makes no claim against Cryptosporidium

claim: Giardia is not claimed from chlorine at 30 minutes; the filter is the barrier for cysts
law: CDC timetable: Giardia about 45 min at 1 mg/L, pH 7.5, 25 C
check: CT 51 against 45: margin 1.13 at 25 C, and the cold-water Giardia CT is several times higher, so no claim is made

claim: Chlorination is only for water under 50 NTU, and settled water does best (under 5 NTU)
law: IFRC tablet-choice note: 0 to 5 NTU low, 5 to 50 NTU high, above 50 NTU do not chlorinate; particles shield microbes and add demand
check: Pictogram: cloudy water, let it settle and pour off, use two tablets; muddy water, do not use D alone (HWP-SRC-001 SC3, SC6); users cannot measure NTU, so the pictogram's see-through test is checked by persona (TH)

claim: The chlorine residual protects the stored household supply from recontamination after it has been filtered
law: CDC SWS: residual above 0.2 mg/L at 24 h is for protection in storage; granular carbon removes free chlorine fast (HWP-CLM-001 sequence: chlorinate, wait, filter, carbon removes taste)
check: Fails as a system: wherever A to C put carbon after the wait, the filtered water carries no residual, and the carbon bed itself can grow heterotrophic bacteria with no chlorine to control it. Fix options change C's design and the program sequence, so they go to Amish (HWD-DEC-001 D3)

claim: A few mg/L of free chlorine ahead of the filter does not harm the hollow-fibre modules of A to C
law: PVDF and PES hollow fibres are commonly cleaned with hypochlorite; tolerance is given by makers as a chlorine exposure in mg h/L, commonly 1e5 to 1e6
check: Even with the fibres soaked in dosed water all year the exposure is about 14,900 mg h/L; the bought module's limit and flux on chlorinated feed are confirmed with the supplier and over 100 L (HWD-DEC-001 C3)

claim: The carbon stages of A to C remove the dosed chlorine taste over their life (B: about 7 g of carbon against about 1.7 mg/L x 150 L = 0.26 g of chlorine)
law: Carbon reduces free chlorine by surface reaction; NSF/ANSI 42 chlorine reduction is the reference test
check: Total capacity is not the limit: 7 g is about 15 mL of bed, a contact time of a few seconds at B's flow, so breakthrough at the real flow and over the module's life in litres is measured (HWP-VER-001 TG)

claim: By-products stay low: cyanuric acid from NaDCC at the double dose is about 4.1 mg/L against the WHO 40 mg/L; THMs from household chlorination have been found below WHO guideline values
law: WHO NaDCC fact sheet (NaDCC 50 mg/L, cyanuric acid 40 mg/L); Lantagne et al. 2008 as summarised by Akvopedia; WHO GDWQ THM guideline values
check: Cyanuric acid holds by arithmetic; THMs at the double dose in organic-rich settled water are the case the field data do not cover, so THMs are measured (TG)

claim: A 20 L tablet cannot enter the blue 1 L well (13 mm tablet against a 9.5 mm bore); it would give 40 mg/L chlorine and 67 mg/L NaDCC in a bottle
law: WHO guideline values 5 mg/L chlorine and 50 mg/L NaDCC; keyed well bores 9.5 mm (1 L) and 14.5 mm (20 L) against assumed tablet sizes 8 and 13 mm
check: Fixed as briefed (F2, colour-keyed inserts); the key blocks the well only, so a 20 L tablet dropped straight into an open bottle neck is a misuse the cap cannot stop: the 20 L tablets ship only in the household kit, strips are matched to the insert colours where the supplier allows, and the label warns (HWD-RSK-001); tablet sizes are measured before the bores are frozen (C1)

claim: No more than two tablets fit in the well, so the dose cannot pass the 5 mg/L guideline value (three 1 L tablets would give 6 mg/L)
law: Free height under the plug stop 8.0 mm (1 L) and 11.0 mm (20 L) against tablets 3.5 and 5.0 mm thick (assumed)
check: Two fit (7.0 under 8.0 mm); three are stopped only while each tablet is thicker than 2.67 mm (1 L) or 3.67 mm (20 L); the minimum thickness is measured (C1) and the plug stop set from it; broken tablets are a misuse on the label

claim: The ball timer works in the Stokes regime: a 2 mm steel ball in about 548,000 cSt silicone falls 13 mm in about 45 min at 25 C
law: Stokes drag with the Haberman-Sayre wall factor 0.1704 at d/D = 0.5 (Faxen, 0.1796, is not valid there); fluid 534 Pa s; PMX-200 type grades exist to 600,000 cSt
check: 1.75835e-08 Reynolds number <= 0.1 Reynolds number

claim: The timer never reads less than 30 minutes up to 40 C air temperature (nominal 45 min at 25 C; 30.3 min at 40 C and -10 % viscosity)
law: Fall time scales with viscosity; viscosity tolerance assumed 10 %; activation energy 15 kJ/mol; the briefed 34 min nominal read 23 min at 40 C
check: 30.3 min >= 30 min

claim: In cold water the user runs the timer twice (10 to 18 C) or three times (under 10 C); the timer itself slows about 1.38 times at 10 C
law: Silicone viscosity-temperature coefficient 0.61 (Dow PMX-200), which back-calculates to the assumed 15 kJ/mol; contact times as S11
check: Low-tolerance totals at the warm end of each band: 94 min (two runs at 18 C, need 60) and 167 min (three runs at 10 C, need 120). Failed as briefed (one run for all water); fixed by the run count on the label (F4, revised to one, two, three by F11). The user judges water temperature by feel; that is checked by persona (TH)

claim: The 1 L tablet dissolves fully in the well when the bottle is turned over and shaken, and the clear plug shows it has gone
law: NaDCC household tablets are effervescent; floor slots let raw water flood the well when inverted; the CO2 vents through the slots
check: Dissolution time in the well at 5 and 30 C to measure (TJ); the pictogram says shake until the tablet has gone, then start the timer; the 20 L route cannot be inverted and is S41

claim: The well insert O-ring is squeezed within the static-seal range in the 20.4 mm bore over the stated tolerances (15.1 to 28.0 %, nominal 21.9 %)
law: Static radial gland: squeeze 15 to 30 %; groove root 17.9 mm; bore +/-0.05 mm, groove +/-0.03 mm, section 1.6 +/-0.08 mm (ISO 3601 class); stretch 4.1 %
check: Failed as briefed twice: root 17.2 gave 0 %, and root 17.8 at print tolerance (+/-0.1 mm) gave 7.9 % at the low end. Fixed (F5, F10): root 17.9 mm, the bore and groove held to the stated tolerances (moulded at scale; the prototype insert is measured and reprinted to the gauge)

claim: The cap screws onto the same 28 mm PCO 1881 neck as the B cartridge and onto the 28 mm port proposed for C's raw-bucket lid
law: PCO 1881 neck data (Kapy CAD), as used in HWB-CAL-001; C's lid port is a proposal to solution C
check: The bottle neck interface follows HWB; the C port is not yet agreed, so the row stays open until the interface is agreed (HWD-DEC-001 D4)

claim: Every wetted material resists dilute chlorine and the tablet concentrate in the well, and is available in a drinking-water listed grade (PP, silicone, EPDM, PETG)
law: NSF/ANSI/CAN 61 (HWP-REG-001 W7); polyolefins and EPDM resist dilute hypochlorite; PC is prone to stress cracking in alkaline hypochlorite
check: While a tablet dissolves the well briefly holds about 0.0 g/L (1 L) to 0.0 g/L (20 L) of chlorine; the clear plug is PETG or clarified PP, not PC (F12); printed prototype grades are not listed, so prototypes see known potable test water only; concentrate soak and leachables to test (TG)

claim: Tablets keep 3 to 5 years in their strips; the cap stores no tablets loose
law: Akvopedia: strips 5 years, tubs 3 years; humidity degrades NaDCC once the foil is open
check: One tablet is taken from the strip per use; spare strips ride in the kit, not in the cap

claim: Freezing and heat do not damage the tablets or the timer, and a frozen bottle is thawed before dosing
law: Water expands about 9 % on freezing; PDMS stays liquid far below 0 C and expands 9.6e-04 per K (Dow PMX-200)
check: Water left in the well could crack the clear plug if frozen: empty the cap in freezing weather. The sealed timer holds 0.188 mL; from a 25 C fill its fluid changes by -6.3 to +6.3 uL over -10 to 60 C (3.4%), enough to load the end caps or open a bubble; an expansion allowance is to be detailed and a freeze-thaw and 60 C fall-time test run (C5, TI)

claim: A child or an older user can open a foil strip, drop a tablet in, turn the plug (3.5 turns) and flip the timer the counted number of times
law: Low-dexterity users struggle with small parts and caps (HWP-PRB-001 personas)
check: To observe by persona (HWP-VER-001 TH) with pass criteria: dose done in under 2 minutes, no tablet dropped, the right run count chosen; a strip with a tear notch and a 27 mm knurled plug are specified

claim: D1 weighs under 60 g without the bottle (45 g, model volumes)
law: Model volumes x densities (cad_parts.MATERIALS), per part in cad/fidelity.json

claim: CDC SWS arithmetic: 3 mL of 1.25 % hypochlorite in 20 L is about 1.9 mg/L
check: claimed 1.875 mg/L, estimate 1.88 mg/L (ratio 1.00)

claim: D1 prototype parts and test tablets cost under the USD 10 value-engineering target (USD 9.15)
law: BOM sum (bom/bom.csv); estimates, not quotes
check: 9.15 USD <= 10 USD

claim: D2: the metering chamber holds 3.01 mL below the standpipe top, within 5 % of the CDC 3.0 mL dose for 20 L
law: Annulus area (18 mm chamber, 5 mm standpipe) x 12.8 mm standpipe height; tilt and wall film are not modelled and the dose is weighed at TRL 4
check: 0.006 mL from 3.0 <= 0.15 mL from 3.0

claim: D2: 5 drops from a 2.0 mm orifice treat 1 L at 1.7 to 2.1 mg/L
law: Tate's law with the Harkins-Brown factor 0.60 to 0.72; LDPE does not wet, so the drop pins at the orifice: 0.0277 to 0.0332 mL per drop
check: Failed as briefed: three drops from a 1.2 mm orifice give 0.62 to 0.75 mg/L, under 1. Fixed (F9): 2.0 mm orifice and five drops; drops weighed gravimetrically at TRL 4; a squeezed stream is the misuse on the label

claim: D2: the liquid loses strength over its shelf life (a warm-storage bound gives 56% after 3 months, so one cap gives 1.0 mg/L, and 0.58 mg/L at 6 months)
law: WEDC: half strength in a year when cool and dark; E4C WaterGuard: 13 % to 8 % in 75 days at 27 C (a bound for 1.25 %); Akvopedia: use within 3 months
check: Under-dosing as the liquid ages is a silent failure the user cannot see; D2 would need a date stamp, a 3 month use-by and a two-cap rule after 2 months (scored in HWD-OPT-001)

claim: D2: a gentle squeeze lifts the liquid into the chamber (about 1.8 kPa) well within a weak child's grip
law: Hydrostatic lift of 134 mm plus 0.5 kPa entry loss; grip 124 N weak child (Camry norms, as HWB-CAL-001); squeeze force assumed 10 N

claim: D2: 1.25 % hypochlorite is an irritant, not a corrosive at that strength, and is kept behind a child-resistant flip cap
law: CDC SWS uses 1.25 % for household distribution; under CLP generic limits 1 to 5 % of a Skin Corr. 1B substance classes as Skin Irrit. 2 and Eye Irrit. 2
check: Hazard handled in HWD-RSK-001 (eye splash at pH about 12, child access); D1 tablets carry a do-not-swallow warning on the strip (IFRC)

claim: A 1 L tablet put in the orange 20 L well by mistake is noticed (it would give 0.1 mg/L, two give 0.2 mg/L)
law: An 8 mm tablet passes a 14.5 mm bore; the key works one way only; WHO 0.5 mg/L after 30 min
check: A silent under-dose: mitigated by actual-size tablet circles on the label next to each insert, the clear plug, and 20 L tablets packed only with the household kit; a free chlorine check after the wait would catch it (D7); misuse trial (TH)

claim: On C's bucket port the 20 L tablet dissolves and mixes through the 20 L without turning the bucket over
law: A 20 kg bucket cannot be inverted and shaken; a dissolved dose entering at the surface mixes slowly without stirring
check: Failed as briefed (the inversion method was written for bottles). Fixed (F7): on the bucket the plug is taken off and raw water is poured through the well from a cup until the tablet has gone, then the bucket is stirred for 30 s with a clean stick before the timer starts; free chlorine at top and bottom after 1 and 5 minutes within 20 % of the mean (TJ); the simpler drop-in-before-filling method is put to Amish under D4

claim: The 1 L tablet is used only in bottles of 1 to 1.5 L, so a clear single dose gives at least 1.33 mg/L and a double dose at most 4.0 mg/L
law: Dose = 2 mg / volume: 0.5 L gives 4.0 and 8.0 mg/L (double over 5); 2 L gives 1.0 mg/L; range printed on the blue insert label (F8)
check: 4 mg/L <= 5 mg/L

claim: A wrong, missing, weak or undissolved dose is visible to the user before the water is filtered
law: Free chlorine is invisible; the clear plug shows only that the tablet has gone; DPD test strips or a comparator read 0.2 mg/L and above
check: Fails as designed: there is no field check of the residual after the wait. Fix proposed: a pack of free chlorine test strips in each kit and a check after the wait (target at least 0.5 mg/L); it changes the kit and its cost, so it goes to Amish (HWD-DEC-001 D7)
